experiences.name: Meia Praia Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed afternoon at Meia Praia, one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, located just minutes from Lagos town center. Ideal for a late Day 1 arrival — simply drop bags at a Lagos-based hotel and walk to the beach. Calm waters, golden sand, and beachside bars make it perfect for unwinding after a long flight without needing transport.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim
experiences.description: Explore the iconic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear coves of Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Stay in Carvoeiro or Lagoa to be within 10 minutes of this spot, avoiding long transfers. Morning visits offer calmer waters and fewer crowds, perfect for snorkeling and cliff photography.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a local quinta near Lagoa, the heart of Algarve wine country, sampling regional Negra Mole and Arinto wines paired with fresh local seafood and cheeses. Sessions typically run 2–3 hours and are hosted mid-morning, making them ideal for Day 2 or 3 when you are fully settled. Book a hotel in Lagoa or Silves to be within 15 minutes of multiple quintas.

experiences.name: Silves Castle and Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Discover the Moorish Silves Castle and wander the cobblestone streets of Portugal's former Algarve capital. Combine culture with food by joining a guided walking tour that stops at local taverns for regional wines, cataplana seafood stew, and medronho brandy. Silves is centrally located and easily reachable from Lagoa or Carvoeiro hotels in under 20 minutes, keeping transfers short and maximizing your day.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the famous Benagil Cave, one of the Algarve's most spectacular natural wonders, on a guided kayak tour departing directly from Benagil Beach. Tours last approximately 2 hours and depart in the morning when seas are calmest. Stay in Carvoeiro, just 5 km away, to avoid long travel and ensure you catch the early morning slot before afternoon winds pick up. A highlight activity well within budget.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €5-7, ~1.5 hours). Check into Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack from a nearby convenience store or a slice of pizza from a late-night spot near the hostel. Budget: €3-5

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Faro to Lagos bus ticket online to save time. The hostel is centrally located in Lagos, making it easy to walk to most attractions. Keep luggage light for the bus journey.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hostel or a nearby pastelaria. Stroll through Lagos old town, explore the historic city walls, and visit the free Igreja de Santa Maria church in the main square (Praça Gil Eanes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Meia Praia Beach (about 2 km from the hostel or a short bus ride). This long, wide sandy beach is perfect for swimming and relaxing. It's less crowded than the famous grottos beaches and completely free to access.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Lagos town center. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril for budget dining options. Enjoy a sunset stroll along the marina.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mulher de Capote near the town center — coffee and pastel de nata for €2-3
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local Mercado de Lagos (fresh bread, cheese, fruit) for €4-6
meals.dinner: O Camilo or a local tasca on Rua 25 de Abril — prato do dia (dish of the day) with soup, main, and drink for €8-10

day_by_day.notes: September is still warm and sunny in the Algarve (avg 25°C), perfect beach weather. Bring sunscreen and a reusable water bottle to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Ponta da Piedade — a stunning coastal rock formation just 2 km south of Lagos. Walk or rent a bike (€8-10/day from local shops near the hostel). Explore the clifftop trails and viewpoints for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the steps to the sea caves and grottos at Ponta da Piedade. Hire a local fisherman's boat tour of the grottos (€10-15 per person, negotiate directly with the boat operators at the bottom of the steps for the best price). Visit Praia do Camilo nearby — a small, beautiful beach accessible via wooden steps.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Visit the Mercado de Escravos (Slave Market Museum) — entry is around €3 — one of the oldest slave markets in Europe, a sobering but important historical site.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast if included, or grab a galão (milky coffee) and tosta mista (toasted sandwich) at a local café for €3
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Ponta da Piedade or bring packed snacks — bifanas (pork sandwiches) from a local café for €2-3
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina near the marina — grilled fish or cataplana for €10-12

day_by_day.notes: Go to Ponta da Piedade early morning to avoid crowds and get the best light for photos. The boat tours are cash only, so bring small bills.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus (EVA Bus, €2-3) to Sagres, the southwestern tip of Portugal. Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) — a historic fortress with stunning Atlantic Ocean views and wind rose.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Cabo de São Vicente (about 6 km from Sagres or take a taxi for €8-10 shared) — the most southwestern point of continental Europe. The lighthouse and cliffs are breathtaking. Explore the small market stalls selling local crafts and dried fish.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Relax at the hostel and socialize with fellow travelers in the common area.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hostel or a café near the bus station — €3-4
meals.lunch: A Sagres restaurant near the fortress — fresh grilled sardines or tuna steak for €9-11
meals.dinner: Self-catering from Pingo Doce supermarket in Lagos — pasta, local cheese, wine for €5-7 total

day_by_day.notes: Buses from Lagos to Sagres run several times daily. Check the EVA Bus schedule in advance. Sagres can be windy even in September, so bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take a bus or rideshare to Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (approx. 30 km east of Lagos). Book a budget wine tasting session in advance (€10-15 per person for 4-5 wines). The Algarve produces excellent local wines including Negra Mole and Crato Branco varieties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue wine exploration at Quinta da Penina or visit the Lagos Wine Cellar (Adega Cooperativa do Algarve) closer to town for a more affordable tasting (€5-8). Purchase a bottle of local wine to enjoy later.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Stroll along the marina at sunset with your purchased wine. Visit the free viewpoint at Forte da Ponta da Bandeira for golden hour views.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha in Lagos town center — coffee and croissant for €2-3
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery if offered, or a nearby café — €8-10
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Vivant in Lagos — affordable Portuguese tapas and wine for €12-15

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to confirm winery opening hours and tasting availability. Some wineries require reservations. Consider sharing a taxi with hostel mates to split costs.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Albufeira (1 hour by bus, €5-6 each way). Visit the old town and the famous Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) — a beautiful beach right in the town center, free to access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Albufeira's sea caves and cliffs. Walk the clifftop path to Praia de São Rafael (about 3 km west) — one of the most scenic beaches in the Algarve with dramatic rock formations. Swim and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Albufeira's old town streets and the lively Rua Cândido dos Reis. Head back to Lagos by evening bus.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or Lagos café before departure — €3
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia dos Pescadores — grilled chicken piri-piri wrap for €6-8
meals.dinner: Back in Lagos — Tasca do Zé or similar local tasca — bacalhau (salt cod) dish for €9-11

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira can be touristy and pricier than Lagos. Stick to local tascas away from the main strip for better value. The bus journey offers scenic Algarve countryside views.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia da Luz, a charming village beach 6 km west of Lagos. Take the local bus (€1.50) or walk along the coastal path. The beach is wide, calm, and less crowded than Lagos beaches. Swim and explore the black rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk back toward Lagos along the scenic coastal cliffs (about 1.5 hours). Stop at Praia do Porto de Mós — a beautiful, quieter beach with golden cliffs. Relax and swim.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Lagos, visit the weekly local market if it falls on this day, or browse the artisan shops on Rua da Barroca. Enjoy a sundowner at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local padaria (bakery) — fresh bread and coffee for €2-3
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia da Luz — fresh fish sandwich and local beer for €7-9
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Dois Irmãos in Lagos — seafood rice or grilled sea bass for €11-13

day_by_day.notes: The coastal walk from Praia da Luz to Lagos is stunning but can be warm. Start early and bring plenty of water. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve (30 min by train from Lagos, €3-4 each way). Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry) with panoramic views over the orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves Cathedral (Sé de Silves, free entry) and the charming old town streets. Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia (€2 entry). Walk along the Arade River banks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the hostel common area. Try some of the local wine purchased earlier in the trip.

meals.breakfast: Quick café stop before catching the train — galão and pastel de nata for €2-3
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for affordable grilled chicken and local specialties, €10-12
meals.dinner: Self-catering at the hostel — local cheese, presunto (cured ham), olives, and bread from the supermarket for €5-6

day_by_day.notes: The train from Lagos to Silves is scenic and very affordable. Check the CP (Comboios de Portugal) schedule. Silves is quieter and more authentic than coastal towns — a great contrast.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Dona Ana — one of Lagos's most photographed beaches, just 1.5 km from the hostel. Arrive early to secure a good spot. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water surrounded by golden limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the clifftop trail from Praia de Dona Ana toward Ponta da Piedade (already visited on Day 3, but the trail itself is worth doing in full). Stop at hidden coves and viewpoints along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Ponta da Piedade viewpoint. Return to Lagos for dinner. Visit the lively Rua 25 de Abril for evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hostel — scrambled eggs on toast and coffee for €4-5
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia de Dona Ana — fresh orange juice and a sandwich for €5-6
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Galeão in Lagos — traditional Portuguese pork or fish dishes for €10-12

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Dona Ana has limited shade, so bring an umbrella or arrive early. The clifftop trail can be uneven in places — wear sturdy sandals or trainers.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — visit Herdade do Esporão or a local Algarve wine cooperative. Alternatively, join a free or low-cost wine and food pairing workshop sometimes offered at local wine shops in Lagos town center. Ask at the hostel for current recommendations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lagos Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal) for fresh local produce, cheeses, and regional products. Pick up affordable souvenirs like local honey, fig jam, or medronho (arbutus berry spirit). Explore the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a communal dinner at the hostel kitchen using market ingredients — a great way to save money and meet fellow travelers. Make a simple cataplana-inspired dish with clams, tomatoes, and local wine.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen — toast, local jam, and coffee for €2
meals.lunch: Market snacks — olives, local cheese, fresh bread for €4-5
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hostel meal — ingredients from the market for €6-8 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos Municipal Market is best visited in the morning when produce is freshest. Cooking at the hostel is a great budget strategy and a fun social activity.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha (20 min by bus from Lagos, €2-3). Praia da Rocha is one of the Algarve's most famous beaches — a long stretch of golden sand with dramatic orange rock formations. Arrive early to enjoy it before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Portimão town center. Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sunday afternoons, €3 other times) — an excellent museum in a converted sardine canning factory. Walk along the Arade River waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Try Portimão's famous grilled sardines at one of the riverside restaurants — a local specialty and very affordable. Return to Lagos by bus.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagos before departure — €3
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia da Rocha — fresh fruit and a bifana for €5-6
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Portimão — grilled sardines, bread, and local wine for €9-11

day_by_day.notes: Portimão is famous for its sardine festival (usually in August, but the tradition continues). The grilled sardines here are considered among the best in Portugal — don't miss them!

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final relaxed morning at your favorite Lagos beach — Praia de Dona Ana, Meia Praia, or Praia do Camilo. Take a long swim and soak up the last of the Algarve sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore any remaining Lagos sights — the Forte da Ponta da Bandeira (€3 entry, a 17th-century fort at the marina entrance), or revisit the old town for last-minute souvenir shopping. Visit the local artisan market if available.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos. Splurge slightly on a nicer meal to celebrate the trip. Visit a local wine bar for a final Algarve wine tasting — try a glass of local Moscatel dessert wine.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or similar — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, toast, and coffee for €5-6
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach snack bar — grilled fish and salad for €9-10
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina or similar — splurge on a cataplana (traditional Algarve seafood stew) for €15-18, shared between two

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do any last-minute shopping, pack, and prepare for departure. Check bus/train times to Faro Airport for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Boutique Taghostel. Store luggage at the hostel if needed for a few hours. Take a final morning walk through Lagos old town — visit the Igreja de Santo António (€3 entry, stunning gilded baroque interior) if not visited earlier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Faro Airport via EVA Bus or Rede Expressos from Lagos bus station (€5-7, ~1.5 hours). Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for the journey and check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the Algarve's beaches, wines, and culture.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and coffee at a Lagos café — €2-3
meals.lunch: Snack at Faro Airport or pack leftovers from the hostel — €5-8
meals.dinner: On the flight or at the destination

day_by_day.notes: Keep your bus ticket receipt in case of any issues. The Lagos to Faro bus is reliable but book in advance during peak season. Leave a review for the hostel — it helps other budget travelers!

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take the airport shuttle or a pre-booked taxi (~45 min, ~€50) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and grab a late-night snack near the hostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Late-night bite at a nearby tasca or grab takeaway from a local kebab or snack bar open late in Lagos town center (~€8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you're arriving late. Confirm your check-in with Boutique Taghostel in advance as it's after 22:00. Pack light for easy airport-to-hotel transfer. Rest well for the adventures ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Start your first full day with a leisurely breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café. Then take a short walk to explore Lagos Old Town — stroll through Praça Gil Eanes, visit the Igreja de Santo António (a stunning baroque church), and get your bearings in this charming coastal town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia Beach Day experience — one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, just a 10-minute taxi or water taxi ride from Lagos marina. Enjoy the calm Atlantic waters, golden sand, and relaxed beach atmosphere. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella (~€10–15) and spend the afternoon swimming and unwinding.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for sunset drinks at a rooftop bar or terrace overlooking the marina. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril for dinner options.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a local pastelaria near the hostel — coffee, pastel de nata, and toast (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Meia Praia — grilled sardines, salad, and a cold Sagres beer (~€15–20)
meals.dinner: O Camilo or Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — fresh grilled fish or cataplana de marisco (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Water taxi from Lagos marina to Meia Praia runs regularly in summer/early autumn (~€2 each way). September weather in the Algarve is typically warm (24–28°C) and sunny — ideal beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take a local bus or taxi (~25 min) to Lagoa to join the Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience at a local quinta. This guided tasting session introduces you to the region's indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Arinto, paired with local seafood delicacies. Learn about Algarve's unique wine-making traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine experience into the early afternoon, then explore the town of Lagoa briefly — visit the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa, one of the oldest wine cooperatives in Portugal, to pick up a bottle or two as souvenirs. Return to Lagos by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hostel or take an evening walk along Lagos' city walls and waterfront promenade. Enjoy a quiet dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or Pastelaria Mota in Lagos — fresh bread, cheese, ham, and coffee (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Included or partially included in the wine and seafood pairing experience at the quinta (~€35–50 per person for the full experience)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Vivant or Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and local wine (~€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience in advance as spots fill up quickly, especially in September. Arrange transport to Lagoa ahead of time — a taxi or Uber is most convenient (~€15 each way).

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning bus or taxi to Silves (~30 min from Lagos) for the Silves Castle and Old Town Food Walk experience. Begin with a visit to the impressive red sandstone Moorish Silves Castle, which offers panoramic views over the Algarve countryside. Explore the castle's ramparts, towers, and the archaeological museum inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the guided Old Town Food Walk through Silves' cobblestone streets — taste local specialties like medronho (arbutus berry brandy), almond sweets, smoked sausages, and regional cheeses. Visit the Silves Cathedral (Sé de Silves), one of the finest Gothic churches in the Algarve. Browse artisan shops for local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and perhaps a glass of wine at a wine bar in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hostel before departing — yogurt, fruit, and coffee (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Tastes included in the food walk, supplemented by a sit-down lunch at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for its cataplana (~€20–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Vasco da Gama or A Forja restaurant in Lagos — traditional Portuguese pork or bacalhau dishes (~€18–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is easily reached by bus from Lagos (Eva Transportes, ~€3.50 each way) or by taxi (~€20). The Silves Medieval Fair typically takes place in August, but the castle and old town are equally atmospheric in September with fewer crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Praia da Marinha for the Cliff Walk and Swim experience. Catch a bus or taxi to Carvoeiro (~40 min), then walk or take a local taxi to Praia da Marinha. Begin the iconic cliff walk along the golden limestone formations, sea arches, and hidden grottos. The scenery is among the most photographed in all of Portugal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the beach for a swim in the crystal-clear turquoise coves. Explore the sea caves by renting a kayak or joining a short boat tour from the beach (~€15–20). Spend the afternoon soaking in the dramatic coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Lagos via Carvoeiro village — stop for a sunset drink at a clifftop bar in Carvoeiro before returning to Lagos for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hostel — croissant, fresh orange juice, and espresso (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia da Marinha or pack a picnic from a Lagos supermarket — sandwiches, fruit, and water (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Galeão or Mullens in Lagos — grilled sea bass or tuna steak with local wine (~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is about 25 km east of Lagos. The cliff walk can be slippery — wear sturdy shoes. Arrive early to secure a spot on the small beach. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slower morning in Lagos. Visit the Mercado Municipal de Lagos (local market) for fresh produce, local cheeses, and regional products. Then walk down to Praia Dona Ana — a stunning small beach with dramatic rock formations just 10 minutes from the hostel — for a morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak or join a guided sea cave tour from Praia Dona Ana or Praia do Camilo (~€25–35 per person). Paddle through the famous Ponta da Piedade sea arches and grottos — one of the most spectacular natural sights in the Algarve. Alternatively, take a boat tour from Lagos marina (~€20–30).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll back to Lagos town center for a leisurely evening. Visit a local wine shop to pick up a bottle of Algarve wine and enjoy it on the hostel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast — fresh fruit, local bread, and cheese from the Mercado Municipal (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia Dona Ana or Restaurante Piri Piri in Lagos — piri piri chicken and salad (~€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso or Restaurante Nah Nah Bah in Lagos — burgers, wraps, or local fusion dishes for a more casual evening (~€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is best visited by kayak or boat for the full experience. Book sea cave tours in advance during September as they remain popular. The market is open mornings only, Monday–Saturday.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres — the southwestern tip of Portugal and one of Europe's most dramatic coastal landscapes. Take a bus from Lagos (~1 hour, ~€4) or rent a car for the day. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress perched on dramatic cliffs where Henry the Navigator once planned his voyages of discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Cabo de São Vicente — the most southwesterly point of mainland Europe — where towering cliffs meet the Atlantic Ocean. Visit the lighthouse and enjoy the raw, windswept scenery. Walk along the clifftops and watch surfers tackle the powerful Atlantic swells at nearby Praia do Tonel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by early evening. Enjoy a well-deserved dinner and a glass of wine to celebrate the midpoint of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or a café in Lagos before departure (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: A Sagres restaurant such as Restaurante O Telheiro do Infante — fresh grilled fish with ocean views (~€18–24 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — seafood rice or grilled octopus with Algarve white wine (~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is about 30 km west of Lagos. Renting a car for this day gives you more flexibility to explore Cabo de São Vicente and the surrounding beaches. It can be windy at the cape even in September — bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the hostel — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and plan the second half of your trip. Then take a short walk to Praia do Meia Praia for a morning swim and beach walk. This is a great day to recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu de Lagos (Lagos Museum) in the afternoon — housed in a former convent, it covers the town's history from prehistoric times through the Age of Discovery. Then browse the boutique shops and galleries along Rua Cândido dos Reis for local art, ceramics, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Join a sunset sailing trip from Lagos marina (~€35–45 per person, 2 hours) — a magical way to see the Algarve coastline from the water as the sun dips below the horizon. Return for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or Café Apolo in Lagos — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, bread, and coffee (~€7–10)
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Meia Praia or a light lunch at a café in Lagos town center — soup, sandwich, and juice (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — sharing plates of local cheeses, cured meats, and seafood petiscos with Algarve wine (~€20–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sunset sailing trips depart from Lagos marina — book in advance. The Lagos Museum is closed on Mondays. This is a good day to do laundry at the hostel if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip east to Portimão and Praia da Rocha. Catch a bus from Lagos (~30 min, ~€3). Start with a visit to the Museu de Portimão — an award-winning museum built inside a former sardine canning factory, offering fascinating insight into the region's fishing heritage. Free or low-cost entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Praia da Rocha — a wide, golden beach backed by dramatic ochre cliffs. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and exploring the clifftop promenade. Visit the Fortaleza de Santa Catarina at the eastern end of the beach for views over the Arade River estuary.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Portimão's waterfront for dinner — the riverside area is famous for its sardine restaurants. Return to Lagos by bus or taxi in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hostel in Lagos before departure (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia da Rocha or a café on the clifftop promenade — grilled sardines, salad, and beer (~€14–18)
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré or Restaurante Titanic on Portimão's waterfront — grilled sardines or dourada (sea bream) with local wine (~€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Portimão is one of the Algarve's largest towns and has excellent transport links from Lagos. The Museu de Portimão is one of the best free/low-cost cultural experiences in the region — don't miss it.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Algarve wine country for a deeper exploration. Take a taxi or rent a car and visit Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar (~30 min from Lagos) — one of the Algarve's most acclaimed wine estates. Join a morning vineyard tour and tasting session, exploring the estate's sculpture garden and cellars.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the wine tour, drive or taxi to the nearby town of Estômbar or Ferragudo — a picturesque fishing village on the Arade River estuary. Wander the whitewashed streets, visit the 16th-century castle ruins, and enjoy the authentic, less-touristy atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a relaxed evening. Visit a local wine bar to compare your Algarve wine discoveries from the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or a pastelaria in Lagos (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Quinta dos Vales or a café in Ferragudo — local bread, cheese, and wine (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Sueste in Ferragudo (if still there in the evening) or back in Lagos at Restaurante Bon Vivant — fresh fish and Algarve wine (~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales offers tours and tastings — book ahead online. Ferragudo is a hidden gem compared to busier Algarve towns and is well worth the short detour. A rental car makes this day much easier.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Praia de Odeceixe — a stunning beach at the northern tip of the Algarve where a river meets the sea, creating a unique lagoon-like environment. It's about 1 hour from Lagos by car or bus. Arrive early to enjoy the peaceful atmosphere before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon swimming in the river lagoon or the Atlantic, exploring the dramatic cliffs, and walking the coastal trails. The village of Odeceixe above the beach is charming — grab a coffee and browse the small shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by late afternoon. Enjoy a final evening exploring any remaining spots in Lagos you haven't visited — perhaps the city walls at sunset or a live music venue.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel before departure (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Cego in Odeceixe village or a snack bar near the beach — grilled fish, salad, and local wine (~€16–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Forja in Lagos — traditional Portuguese meat and fish dishes in a cozy setting (~€20–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Odeceixe is technically in the Alentejo coast region but is easily accessible from Lagos. The beach is part of the Costa Vicentina Natural Park — one of the most unspoiled coastlines in Western Europe. A rental car is strongly recommended for this day.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your penultimate morning revisiting your favorite beach — whether Praia Dona Ana, Meia Praia, or Praia do Camilo (a dramatic small beach with wooden staircase access, just south of Lagos). Take a final morning swim and soak in the Algarve sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a final afternoon of souvenir shopping and exploration. Visit the Mercado Municipal one last time for local products — almond sweets, medronho, local wine, and ceramics make great gifts. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos — choose your favorite restaurant from the trip or try somewhere new. Celebrate 13 days in the Algarve with a bottle of local wine and a memorable meal.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or hostel breakfast — a final pastel de nata and galão (milky coffee) (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café or snack bar near the beach — toasted sandwich, soup, and juice (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for the farewell dinner at Restaurante O Camilo or Restaurante Adega da Marina — full seafood spread with Algarve wine (~€28–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check out procedures with Boutique Taghostel — confirm your checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for the final day. Book your airport transfer in advance for Day 13.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast in Lagos. Take a final stroll along the waterfront promenade and marina, or sit at a café and watch the town come to life. Pick up any last-minute items from local shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Boutique Taghostel (if not already done). Depending on your departure flight time, take a pre-booked taxi or shuttle to Faro Airport (~45–60 min, ~€50–60). Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, wine, seafood, history, and Algarve sunshine.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a Lagos café — fresh orange juice, coffee, and pastries (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a café near the airport if time allows (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer the day before to avoid stress on departure day. Faro Airport (FAO) is approximately 75 km east of Lagos. Keep your wine and medronho purchases in checked luggage. Obrigado e boa viagem — thank you and safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Meia Praia Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed afternoon at Meia Praia, one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, located just minutes from Lagos town center. Ideal for a late Day 1 arrival — simply drop bags at a Lagos-based hotel and walk to the beach. Calm waters, golden sand, and beachside bars make it perfect for unwinding after a long flight without needing transport.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim
experiences.description: Explore the iconic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear coves of Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Stay in Carvoeiro or Lagoa to be within 10 minutes of this spot, avoiding long transfers. Morning visits offer calmer waters and fewer crowds, perfect for snorkeling and cliff photography.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a local quinta near Lagoa, the heart of Algarve wine country, sampling regional Negra Mole and Arinto wines paired with fresh local seafood and cheeses. Sessions typically run 2–3 hours and are hosted mid-morning, making them ideal for Day 2 or 3 when you are fully settled. Book a hotel in Lagoa or Silves to be within 15 minutes of multiple quintas.

experiences.name: Silves Castle and Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Discover the Moorish Silves Castle and wander the cobblestone streets of Portugal's former Algarve capital. Combine culture with food by joining a guided walking tour that stops at local taverns for regional wines, cataplana seafood stew, and medronho brandy. Silves is centrally located and easily reachable from Lagoa or Carvoeiro hotels in under 20 minutes, keeping transfers short and maximizing your day.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the famous Benagil Cave, one of the Algarve's most spectacular natural wonders, on a guided kayak tour departing directly from Benagil Beach. Tours last approximately 2 hours and depart in the morning when seas are calmest. Stay in Carvoeiro, just 5 km away, to avoid long travel and ensure you catch the early morning slot before afternoon winds pick up. A highlight activity well within budget.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) whisks you to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (~1 hour). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of local Algarve wine left by the hotel.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night charcuterie and cheese board arranged by the hotel upon arrival, paired with a glass of Quinta dos Vales white wine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with Boutique Taghostel. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority after a long-haul flight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the hotel. Take a gentle orientation stroll through Lagos old town — explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone lanes to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia Beach Day — one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, just a short taxi or water taxi ride from Lagos marina. Rent a premium sun lounger and parasol, swim in the calm Atlantic waters, and soak in the golden September sun. Arrange a beachside seafood lunch at a top-rated beach restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a sunset aperitivo at a rooftop bar overlooking the marina. Dine at a premium Lagos restaurant specializing in modern Portuguese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — fresh pastries, local cheeses, smoked ham, seasonal fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Grilled sea bass, tiger prawns, and chilled Alvarinho white wine at Restaurante Meia Praia beachside terrace
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at No Pátio (Lagos) — modern Portuguese cuisine with Algarve-sourced ingredients and curated wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Meia Praia is reachable by a 5-minute water taxi from Lagos marina (highly recommended) or a short taxi ride. September weather is typically warm (24–28°C) with calm seas — ideal beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, join the Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience — a guided wine tasting session at a prestigious quinta near Lagoa (~35 minutes from Lagos by private transfer). Explore the vineyards, learn about Algarve's unique wine-producing terroir, and taste award-winning reds, whites, and rosés from the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the experience with a curated seafood pairing lunch at the quinta, matching local wines with freshly prepared Algarve seafood dishes. After lunch, take a private tour of the wine cellar and production facilities before returning to Lagos in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel with a spa treatment or private yoga session (arrange with hotel concierge). Enjoy a quiet, intimate dinner at a boutique wine bar in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Seafood and wine pairing lunch at the quinta — included in the experience (octopus carpaccio, grilled clams, cataplana de marisco paired with Quinta dos Vales and Adega do Cantor wines)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Casinha do Petisco (Lagos) — intimate wine bar with exceptional Portuguese small plates and an extensive local wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience in advance as group sizes are limited. Arrange a private driver for the day for maximum comfort and flexibility. Designated driver essential for the wine tasting.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast, then depart by private transfer to Praia da Marinha (~45 minutes east of Lagos). Begin the Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk — explore the iconic golden limestone cliffs, hidden sea arches, and dramatic rock formations along one of Europe's most beautiful coastal paths. The morning light is spectacular for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the crystal-clear coves for a swim in the turquoise waters. Hire a private kayak or paddleboard to explore the sea caves and grottos accessible from the beach. Enjoy a picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by the hotel or a nearby beach café.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Lagos via Carvoeiro village — stop for a sunset drink at a clifftop bar. Return to Lagos for a premium dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket prepared by the hotel (artisan bread, local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh fruit, and chilled rosé) enjoyed on the clifftops at Praia da Marinha
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina (Lagos) — celebrated for its fresh Algarve seafood, cataplana dishes, and extensive Portuguese wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy footwear for the cliff walk — the paths can be uneven. Bring reef shoes for swimming among the rocks. Praia da Marinha is consistently rated one of the top 10 beaches in Europe. Arrive early to secure the best cove spots.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning — enjoy a late breakfast at the hotel followed by a private guided tour of Lagos historic old town. Visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), Igreja de Santo António, and the stunning Igreja de Santa Maria. Walk along the ancient Moorish city walls for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private boat charter from Lagos marina for a 3-hour coastal cruise along the Ponta da Piedade grottos — arguably the most dramatic sea cave and arch formations in the Algarve. Swim in secluded coves accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the marina. Dress for a special dinner at one of the Algarve's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel with fresh-squeezed orange juice, eggs Benedict, and local pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch on board the private boat charter — chilled seafood platter, local cheeses, and sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bon Bon Restaurant (Carvoeiro, ~30 min) — Michelin-starred, offering an extraordinary tasting menu with wine pairing showcasing the finest Algarve and Portuguese produce

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter at least 2–3 days in advance. Ponta da Piedade is best experienced in the afternoon when the light illuminates the golden rock formations. The Michelin-starred dinner at Bon Bon requires advance reservation — book as early as possible.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — enjoy a slow breakfast, read by the hotel terrace, or take a gentle yoga session. Visit the Lagos Saturday/Sunday market (Mercado Municipal) for fresh local produce, artisan goods, and regional specialties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Sagres (~30 minutes west of Lagos) — visit the dramatic Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Explore the Sagres Fortress (Fortaleza de Sagres) and walk the windswept clifftops with breathtaking Atlantic views. Visit the famous Farol do Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Sagres sunset — one of the most spectacular in Europe — from the clifftops. Return to Lagos for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Lunch at A Sagres restaurant in Sagres village — fresh grilled fish, percebes (barnacles), and local wine with ocean views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Laranjeira (Lagos) — elegant setting, exceptional cataplana de marisco and regional Algarve specialties

day_by_day.notes: Bring a windproof layer for Cabo de São Vicente — it can be breezy even in September. The sunset at Sagres is a bucket-list experience; arrive at least 30 minutes before sunset to find the best vantage point on the cliffs.

day_by_day.morning: Depart after breakfast for the Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour (~1 hour east of Lagos). Join a premium small-group or private guided kayak tour departing from Benagil Beach. Paddle through the world-famous Benagil Cave — a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight — and explore surrounding grottos and arches.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia do Carvalho — a hidden gem accessible via a short tunnel through the cliffs. Swim and sunbathe in the warm September afternoon. Explore the charming fishing village of Benagil.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Lagos via Lagoa town. Stop for a wine tasting at a local adega (wine cellar) in Lagoa. Return to Lagos for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — early start recommended
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at Restaurante O Litoral (Carvoeiro) — grilled octopus, fresh fish of the day, and chilled Algarve white wine on a terrace overlooking the sea
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vasco da Gama (Lagos) — sophisticated Portuguese cuisine with an emphasis on fresh Atlantic seafood and premium wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil kayak tour in advance — private tours are available for a more exclusive experience. The cave is best visited in the morning when the light shines through the natural skylight. Wear water shoes and bring a dry bag for valuables.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, embark on a day trip to Silves — the Moorish capital of the Algarve (~40 minutes from Lagos). Begin with the Silves Castle and Old Town Food Walk. Explore the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), one of the best-preserved Moorish fortresses in Portugal, with panoramic views over the Arade River valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the food walk through Silves' cobblestone streets — visit the Gothic Cathedral (Sé de Silves), the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia, and sample local specialties at artisan food shops. Visit the famous Silves orange and fig orchards. Explore the riverside promenade along the Arade River.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a private wine and cheese tasting arranged at the hotel, featuring a curated selection of Algarve and Alentejo wines.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui (Silves) — legendary seafood restaurant famous for its cataplana, grilled fish, and extensive wine list; a true Algarve institution
meals.dinner: In-hotel private wine and cheese tasting dinner — curated board of Portuguese cheeses (Serra da Estrela, Azeitão, Queijo de Évora), charcuterie, and 4–5 premium Algarve and Alentejo wines

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a must-visit for history lovers. The castle is particularly impressive and offers excellent views. The food walk can be self-guided or arranged with a private local guide through the hotel concierge. Marisqueira Rui is extremely popular — book ahead.

day_by_day.morning: A full beach day at Praia de Dona Ana — one of Lagos' most beautiful and iconic beaches, just a short walk or taxi from the hotel. Rent premium sun loungers and a parasol. The golden cliffs and turquoise water make this one of the most photogenic beaches in the Algarve.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, explore the sea caves and rock formations at Praia do Camilo (adjacent to Dona Ana) — accessible via a wooden staircase down the cliffs. Alternatively, book a stand-up paddleboard lesson or guided snorkeling session along the Lagos coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar near Ponta da Piedade. Dress up for a special evening dinner in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Ponta da Piedade (Lagos) — fresh grilled fish, seafood rice, and local wine with stunning cliff views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eleven (Lagos) — contemporary fine dining with a creative Portuguese tasting menu and exceptional wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Dona Ana can get busy on weekends — arrive early to secure the best spots. The wooden staircase to Praia do Camilo is steep but manageable. Both beaches are within easy walking distance of the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided jeep safari through the Algarve hinterland — explore the Serra de Monchique mountain range, cork oak forests, and traditional whitewashed villages. Visit the spa town of Caldas de Monchique and the summit of Fóia (902m) — the highest point in the Algarve — for panoramic views stretching to the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Monchique town for lunch and a stroll through the artisan market. Visit a local medronho (arbutus berry brandy) distillery for a tasting. Return to Lagos in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening at the hotel — book an in-room massage or spa treatment. Light, elegant dinner at a Lagos wine bar.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Central (Monchique) — traditional Algarve mountain cuisine featuring roast pork, black pork presunto, and local mountain wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tasca do Celso (Lagos) — intimate, award-winning tasca with exceptional Portuguese small plates, natural wines, and a warm, convivial atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Book the private jeep safari through the hotel concierge. The Serra de Monchique is a completely different landscape from the coast — lush, green, and refreshingly cool. Bring a light layer for the Fóia summit. Medronho is very strong — sip carefully!

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Alvor estuary and village (~15 minutes from Lagos). Explore the beautiful Ria de Alvor nature reserve — a protected wetland teeming with birdlife. Walk the elevated wooden boardwalk through the estuary for stunning views. Visit the charming fishing village of Alvor with its whitewashed houses and Manueline church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Meia Praia Beach for a final relaxed beach session — swimming, reading, and enjoying the warm September sun. Alternatively, book a private sailing lesson or sunset sailing charter from Lagos marina.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner drinks at the hotel rooftop or terrace. Special farewell dinner at the finest restaurant in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante O Barão (Alvor) — fresh seafood, grilled fish, and local wine in a traditional setting overlooking the estuary
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Bon Bon Restaurant (Carvoeiro) or a premium Lagos restaurant — full tasting menu with wine pairing, celebrating the end of an extraordinary Algarve journey

day_by_day.notes: The Alvor boardwalk is excellent for birdwatching — bring binoculars if available. The estuary is a UNESCO-protected area. The sunset sailing charter from Lagos marina is a magical way to spend the final afternoon — book 2–3 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos — slow breakfast at the hotel. Take a nostalgic last walk through Lagos old town, revisiting favorite spots. Browse artisan shops for premium Portuguese souvenirs: hand-painted azulejo tiles, local wines, olive oils, and artisan ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lagos Municipal Market (Mercado de Lagos) for a final taste of local produce. Enjoy a leisurely lunch at a favorite Lagos restaurant. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final sunset aperitivo at the marina or a quiet drink at the hotel bar. Early evening private transfer to Faro Airport if departing tonight, or a final relaxed dinner if staying one more night.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet farewell breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — order everything you loved during the stay
meals.lunch: Final lunch at Restaurante Adega da Marina (Lagos) — a beloved Lagos classic for fresh seafood and Portuguese wine
meals.dinner: Light farewell dinner at the hotel bar or a casual Lagos bistro, depending on departure schedule

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours for the private transfer to Faro Airport. Confirm checkout time with the hotel. Consider shipping any wine purchases home via a specialist wine courier to avoid baggage issues.

day_by_day.morning: If still in Lagos — final morning swim at Praia de Dona Ana or Meia Praia for one last Atlantic dip. Enjoy a final coffee and pastel de nata at a Lagos café. Check out of Boutique Taghostel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport. Depart Portugal with extraordinary memories of the Algarve's golden cliffs, crystal waters, world-class wines, and exceptional cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 unforgettable days in one of Europe's most beautiful coastal destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a Lagos café — galão coffee, fresh orange juice, and pastel de nata
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a restaurant near the airport if time permits
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Faro Airport at least 2.5 hours before international departure. The private transfer from Lagos to Faro takes approximately 55–70 minutes depending on traffic. Consider joining the TAP Air Portugal Miles & Go program or similar for future Portugal trips. Obrigado e boa viagem!
